{
  "claim": {
    "weak": "For every asymptotically flat, vacuum, 4-dimensional initial data set (Σ, h, K) satisfying the dominant energy condition (here automatic in vacuum), with Σ diffeomorphic to R^3 and with generic (non-degenerate, non-symmetric) data, the maximal globally hyperbolic development (MGHD) (M, g) contains a future incomplete causal geodesic whose terminal indecomposable past set (TIP) is not contained in the domain of outer communications (DOC); equivalently, the future Cauchy horizon of the DOC is non-empty and the spacetime is future null geodesically incomplete in the black-hole region, so that singularities are hidden from null infinity.",
    "strong": "For every asymptotically flat, vacuum, 4-dimensional initial data set (Σ, h, K) satisfying the dominant energy condition, with Σ diffeomorphic to R^3 and with generic data, the maximal globally hyperbolic development (M, g) is future null geodesically incomplete, and no future-directed causal curve from the DOC reaches future null infinity after entering the black-hole region; moreover, the spacetime is inextendible as a C^0 metric (or at least as a C^2 metric) beyond the Cauchy horizon, so that the singularity is not removable by any extension preserving the Einstein equations in a weak sense."
  },
  "assumptions": {
    "dimension": "4D spacetime (3+1 split)",
    "matter": "vacuum Einstein equations, R_{μν}=0; dominant energy condition holds trivially",
    "initial_data_topology": "Σ is diffeomorphic to R^3, connected, orientable, with one asymptotically flat end",
    "asymptotic_flatness": "Initial data (h, K) satisfy standard asymptotically flat fall-off conditions: h_{ij} - δ_{ij} = O(1/r), K_{ij} = O(1/r^2), with appropriate derivatives, and ADM mass M_ADM > 0",
    "genericity": "The initial data are generic in the sense that they avoid a measure-zero set of solutions with extra Killing fields, time-symmetric data, or non-degenerate trapped surfaces; more precisely, the data are not stationary, not spherically symmetric, and the black-hole interior contains no closed trapped surfaces that are marginally outer trapped with vanishing shear in a way that prevents curvature blow-up",
    "null_infinity": "The spacetime admits a conformal completion with future null infinity I^+ that is complete, smooth, and has topology S^2 × R; the DOC is the set of points causally connected to I^+",
    "visibility": "A singularity is visible if there exists a future-directed causal curve from the singularity to I^+; weak cosmic censorship requires that no such curve exists from the singular boundary of the MGHD",
    "singularity": "A singularity is defined as future null geodesic incompleteness of the MGHD; the singular boundary is the set of terminal indecomposable past/future sets (TIPs/TIFs) not contained in the DOC",
    "extension_regularity": "For weak censorship, the MGHD is inextendible as a C^0 metric; for strong censorship, the MGHD is inextendible as a C^2 metric (or as a distributional solution to the Einstein equations) beyond the Cauchy horizon",
    "causality": "The spacetime is globally hyperbolic up to the Cauchy horizon; the DOC is globally hyperbolic and causally simple"
  },
  "conclusion": {
    "weak": "The MGHD contains a future Cauchy horizon H^+(DOC) that is non-empty, and the spacetime is future null geodesically incomplete; however, no causal curve from the singular region reaches I^+, so the singularity is hidden from asymptotic observers.",
    "strong": "The MGHD is future null geodesically incomplete, and the Cauchy horizon is a curvature singularity that cannot be removed by any C^0 (or C^2) extension; thus determinism fails at the Cauchy horizon, but the singularity is not visible from I^+."
  },
  "ambiguities": [
    "Genericity is not precisely defined: the measure-zero set of non-generic data (e.g., time-symmetric, stationary, or with Killing fields) is not specified, so a proof may fail to cover all physically relevant cases.",
    "The topology of the initial data slice is fixed to R^3, but cosmic censorship may require allowing multiple asymptotically flat ends or non-trivial topology (e.g., wormholes), which could invalidate the proof if such data are excluded.",
    "The definition of 'visibility' is ambiguous: it is unclear whether a singularity is visible if a causal curve reaches I^+ from the singular boundary, or if it suffices that the curve reaches arbitrarily large r, and whether the curve must be future-directed and causal or can be null.",
    "The regularity of the extension is not fixed: weak censorship may require C^0 inextendibility, while strong censorship may require C^2 or distributional inextendibility; a proof that only establishes C^0 inextendibility may not imply strong censorship.",
    "The null infinity structure is assumed to be complete and smooth, but in generic collapse the conformal completion may be only piecewise smooth or may have singular points; a proof that relies on smooth I^+ may not apply to realistic spacetimes."
  ],
  "citations_needed": [
    "Penrose, R. (1969). Gravitational collapse: The role of general relativity. Rivista del Nuovo Cimento, 1, 252–276.",
    "Hawking, S. W., & Penrose, R. (1970). The singularities of gravitational collapse and cosmology. Proceedings of the Royal Society A, 314(1519), 529–548.",
    "Christodoulou, D. (1999). The instability of naked singularities in the gravitational collapse of a scalar field. Annals of Mathematics, 149(1), 183–217.",
    "Wald, R. M. (1997). Gravitational collapse and cosmic censorship. arXiv:gr-qc/9710068.",
    "Dafermos, M. (2005). The interior of charged black holes and the problem of uniqueness in general relativity. Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics, 58(4), 445–504.",
    "Shibata, M., & Sasaki, M. (1999). Black hole formation in the grazing collision of high-energy particles. Physical Review D, 60(8), 084002.",
    "Eardley, D. M., & Smarr, L. (1979). Time functions in numerical relativity: Marginally bound dust collapse. Physical Review D, 19(8), 2239–2259.",
    "Christodoulou, D. (2009). The Formation of Black Holes in General Relativity. EMS Monographs in Mathematics.",
    "Klainerman, S., & Nicolò, F. (2003). The Evolution Problem in General Relativity. Birkhäuser.",
    "Ringström, H. (2009). The Cauchy Problem in General Relativity. EMS Textbooks in Mathematics."
  ]
}
